description: Positive fixture for #1639/#1695: correctness-review's Detect category 6 (unverified runtime/library claim). A docstring asserts bisect.insort is O(log n); the real complexity is O(n) overall (the list.insert shift dominates the O(log n) search), with nothing in the file recording a probe or citation for the claim.

_calibration.note: Measured 2026-08-01 against a live correctness-review dispatch on this fixture: 1 issue, severity suggestion, confidence high, status warn — flagged the O(log n) claim as inaccurate (bisect.insort's insertion step shifts the list and is O(n)). Framed by the agent as a docstring-vs-behavior mismatch rather than literally invoking category 6's 'no recorded probe' wording. ai-provenance-review flagged (#1695 review round) that pinning minConfidenceAnyOf to only high/medium is circular and rewards a spec deviation: agents/correctness-review.md's Confidence table (Exception 2) requires confidence:none for a genuine category-6 finding, since category 6 is evidence-only and must not adjudicate the claim's truth — the measured run's confidence:high did exactly the adjudication the category forbids. 'none' was added to minConfidenceAnyOf so this fixture stays green under EITHER the currently-measured behavior or a future fix that makes the agent correctly emit confidence:none for this case, rather than pinning the non-compliant behavior as the only passing baseline. Disclosure (ai-provenance-review, same review round): {high, medium, none} is the COMPLETE confidence enum per agents/correctness-review.md, so this key no longer discriminates on confidence value at all — it now only asserts the field is present and legal, which it always is for a contract-conforming agent. It is retained as a schema-presence check, not a behavioral one, and is deliberately unpinned until the category-6 confidence-none spec deviation is fixed, at which point it should be narrowed to ["none"].
